text:
nolan: Quick procurement check — I've been running ProcuraIQ through our vendor shortlist. They sent a draft pricing sheet and an email. Need eyes before I reply. High level: hybrid seat+usage model, odd overage terms. Anyone seen this level of complexity recently?

maya: I skimmed the sheet earlier. Main flags: embeddings billed separately, ingestion by GB, and an "active model calls" metric that looks like it could double-charge for streaming.

amanda: I asked them for a sample invoice and a worked example for our baseline usage (we estimated ~500k tokens/mo). Paste from their email below.

amanda (vendor quote): ```ProcuraIQ pricing (excerpt):
- Base platform: $3,000/mo (up to 5 seats)
- Token generation: $0.0008/token up to 50M tokens, $0.0006/token beyond 50M
- Embeddings: $0.002 per vector (default 64-d spec shown) OR $1.75 per 1k vectors depending on plan
- Ingestion: $0.15 per GB of log/metric data
- Throughput overage: $1,000 per additional 100k API requests (measured per-minute burst)
- Annual commit discounts: 15% (12mo), 25% (24mo), 30% (36mo)
Note: Pilot offer — first month waived, months 2–3 at 50% off, pilot excludes SLA/uptime credits.```

jess: From eng POV — the "per vector" vs "per 1k vectors" contradiction is worrying. Our embeddings are 1536 dims for most models (not 64). Need them to clarify whether dimension affects price or if they simply normalize to 1k vectors. Also confirm whether they charge for storing embeddings vs serving them.

nolan: Good points. Amanda can you please: 1) ask them to define "vector" precisely (dims vs normalized unit), 2) request the sample invoice and a calc for our 500k token/month baseline, 3) confirm whether egress or cross-region replication fees apply for Private deployments?

amanda: Sent. Vendor replied this morning: "vectors billed per 1,000 vectors; dims do not change the unit price. Storage is billed separately at $0.05/GB/month. Egress for Private deployments may be billed depending on customer network topology; we'll provide sample invoice lines." They also reiterated the pilot terms but said pilot customers must sign a non-SLA MSA.

maya: We should also think about CAPEX vs OPEX — the base platform fee is material. Legal will want indemnity and data handling language (PII, deletion, access logs). Can procurement-bot create an approval task for this evaluation?

procurement-bot: Task created: PR-2026-089 ProcuraIQ vendor eval. Approvers: maya, nolan, legal, eng lead. Link: https://tools.redwood/approvals/PR-2026-089

jess: Engineering preference: we could use ProcuraIQ only for embeddings and keep generation in-house to control latency/cost. If they route inference to third-party hosts, need explicit data residency guarantees. Also ask about model quantization/precision limits if they host custom models.

nolan: Action items summary: amanda — get sample invoice + clarified pricing (per-vector vs per-1k); maya — check budget alignment and whether we can absorb base fee in Q2; jess — draft data residency and hosting questions for vendor; I'll set a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to decide go/no-go for pilot.

amanda: Will upload invoice workbook to procurement drive as soon as I receive it. Also asked them for a worked example showing our 500k tokens + 100k embedding vectors. :thumbsup:

nolan: Thanks — if the vendor confirms "per 1k vectors" and storage/egress numbers, we should have enough to run the cost model. If anyone gets vendor redlines or a sample MSA, drop it here.

maya: Noted. I'll loop in finance and legal right after the sync.

amanda: Received their workbook (will upload in 5m) — initial glance: they modeled a mid-size plan and showed a monthly cost ~ $9.6k for our baseline (includes base fee + tokens + embeddings + storage). Uploading now.

nolan: Perfect — thanks everyone.
